title: livekit/livekit — End-to-end realtime stack for connecting humans and AI
content:
LiveKit is an open source project that provides scalable, multi-user conferencing based on WebRTC. It's designed to provide everything you need to build real-time video audio data capabilities in your applications.
LiveKit's server is written in Go, using the awesome Pion WebRTC implementation.
Important
If you're building Voice AI, LiveKit Agents is the SDK for code-first realtime voice agents. STT, LLM, TTS, turn detection, expressive speech, keyterm accuracy, tool usage, and telephony all come bundled in the framework. It's available in both Python and Node.js.
# agent.py
from livekit import agents
from livekit.agents import Agent, AgentServer, AgentSession, STTContextOptions, TurnHandlingOptions, inference
server = AgentServer()
@server.rtc_session(agent_name="my-agent")
async def my_agent(ctx: agents.JobContext):
   session = AgentSession(
       stt=inference.STT(model="deepgram/nova-3", language="multi"),
       llm=inference.LLM(model="google/gemma-4-31b-it"),
       tts=inference.TTS(model="inworld/inworld-tts-2", voice="Ashley"),
       turn_handling=TurnHandlingOptions(turn_detection=inference.TurnDetector()),
       stt_context_options=STTContextOptions(keyterms=["LiveKit", "Acme Corp"]),
       expressive=True,
   )
   await session.start(room=ctx.room, agent=Agent(instructions="You are a helpful voice AI assistant."))
   await session.generate_reply(instructions="Greet the user and offer your assistance.")
if __name__ == "__main__":
   agents.cli.run_app(server)
Models come from LiveKit Inference with no per-provider API keys, and LiveKit Cloud handles deployment and observability. Visit the docs for more info at docs.livekit.io/agents.
- Scalable, distributed WebRTC SFU (Selective Forwarding Unit)
- Modern, full-featured client SDKs
- Built for production, supports JWT authentication
- Robust networking and connectivity, UDP/TCP/TURN
- Easy to deploy: single binary, Docker or Kubernetes
- Advanced features including:
  - speaker detection
  - simulcast
  - end-to-end optimizations
  - selective subscription
  - moderation APIs
  - end-to-end encryption
  - SVC codecs (VP9, AV1)
  - webhooks
  - distributed and multi-region
- LiveKit Meet (source)
- Spatial Audio (source)
- Livestreaming from OBS Studio (source)
- AI voice assistant using ChatGPT (source)
- Agents: build real-time multimodal AI applications with programmable backend participants
- Egress: record or multi-stream rooms and export individual tracks
- Ingress: ingest streams from external sources like RTMP, WHIP, HLS, or OBS Studio
Client SDKs enable your frontend to include interactive, multi-user experiences.
Server SDKs enable your backend to generate access tokens, call server APIs, and receive webhooks. In addition, the Go SDK includes client capabilities, enabling you to build automations that behave like end-users.
- CLI - command line interface & load tester
- Docker image
- Helm charts
Tip
We recommend installing LiveKit CLI along with the server. It lets you access server APIs, create tokens, and generate test traffic.
The following will install LiveKit's media server:
brew install livekitcurl -sSL https://get.livekit.io | bash
Download the latest release here
Start LiveKit in development mode by running livekit-server --dev. It'll use a placeholder API key/secret pair.
API Key: devkey
API Secret: secret
To customize your setup for production, refer to our deployment docs
A user connecting to a LiveKit room requires an access token. Access tokens (JWT) encode the user's identity and the room permissions they've been granted. You can generate a token with our CLI:
lk token create \
    --api-key devkey --api-secret secret \
    --join --room my-first-room --identity user1 \
    --valid-for 24h
Head over to our example app and enter a generated token to connect to your LiveKit server. This app is built with our React SDK.
Once connected, your video and audio are now being published to your new LiveKit instance!
lk room join \
    --url ws://localhost:7880 \
    --api-key devkey --api-secret secret \
    --identity bot-user1 \
    --publish-demo \
    my-first-room
This command publishes a looped demo video to a room. Due to how the video clip was encoded (keyframes every 3s), there's a slight delay before the browser has sufficient data to begin rendering frames. This is an artifact of the simulation.
LiveKit Cloud is the fastest and most reliable way to run LiveKit. Every project gets free monthly bandwidth and transcoding credits.
Sign up for LiveKit Cloud.
Read our deployment docs for more information.
Pre-requisites:
- Go 1.23+ is installed
- GOPATH/bin is in your PATH
Then run
git clone https://github.com/livekit/livekit
cd livekit
./bootstrap.sh
mage
We welcome your contributions toward improving LiveKit! Please join us on Slack to discuss your ideas and/or PRs.

report.summary: LiveKit is an open-source Go-based WebRTC and AI infrastructure stack for building scalable realtime voice, video, and data experiences.
report.background: LiveKit started as a scalable WebRTC Selective Forwarding Unit (SFU) for multi-user conferencing and has grown into a complete realtime stack for connecting humans and AI. Its media server is written in Go using Pion WebRTC, offering distributed deployment, JWT authentication, simulcast, end-to-end encryption, SVC codecs, and robust networking over UDP/TCP/TURN. Recognizing demand for voice agents, LiveKit expanded with Agents SDKs for Python and Node.js. These include STT, LLM, TTS, turn detection, expressive speech, keyterm accuracy, tool use, and telephony. The LiveKit Inference layer provides access to multiple models without per-provider API keys, while LiveKit Cloud handles managed deployment, observability, and transcoding.
key_points: LiveKit provides an open-source, production-grade WebRTC SFU written in Go. It supports scalable multi-user video and audio conferencing with features like simulcast, AV1/VP9 SVC codecs, speaker detection, end-to-end encryption, moderation APIs, and multi-region distribution, deployable as a single binary, Docker, or Helm chart.

The LiveKit Agents SDK is designed for code-first realtime voice AI in Python and Node.js. It bundles speech-to-text, LLM reasoning, text-to-speech, turn detection, expressive speech, and telephony into one framework. Model inference can be routed through LiveKit Inference, removing the need to manage multiple API keys.

A full ecosystem exists around the core server: Egress records and streams rooms, Ingress ingests RTMP/WHIP/HLS/OBS sources, and client/server SDKs make frontend and backend integration straightforward. The Go SDK even provides client behavior, letting developers build automated participants, load testing, and test traffic generation via the CLI.

The project is permissively licensed under Apache 2.0 and self-hostable, but LiveKit Cloud offers a managed alternative with free monthly bandwidth and transcoding credits. This lowers the barrier for startups and enterprises to prototype and scale realtime voice agents, virtual classrooms, telephony, or spatial audio applications.
report.impact: For the AI industry, LiveKit creates an open alternative for realtime voice agent infrastructure, comparable to managed telephony and video APIs but with self-hosting options. It also simplifies connecting best-of-breed AI models for STT/LLM/TTS in low-latency sessions. Developers benefit from a faster path to production with turn detection, expressive speech, and tool use already integrated, while retaining control over deployment. Regular users will likely encounter more responsive and natural AI assistants embedded in customer support, healthcare, education, and collaboration tools. By decoupling AI models from transport, LiveKit encourages modular, interoperable realtime applications and reduces vendor lock-in at the infrastructure layer.
report.tools: Try the LiveKit Agents SDK (pip install livekit-agents) and official docs at docs.livekit.io/agents. Explore the livekit/livekit GitHub repo, LiveKit Meet, and lk CLI for load testing. Also watch livekit/egress for recording and livekit/ingress for RTMP/WHIP streaming.
